deep.reconstruction:
The page has four parts. A pencil letter salutation is scribbled in the middle.

(A) Period schemes (top left).
Riemann writes the period scheme of his normalized integrals of the first kind u_1..u_p. The cut a_nu carries pi*i*delta; the cut b_nu carries a_{mu,nu}. This is his 1857 normalization.
Below it is an enlarged (p+1)x(2p+2) scheme. A new row is added for an extra function v (an integral of the third kind, the bracketed symbol at the left). It has the modulus pi*i at the new a-cut. Its b-moduli are alpha_nu - beta_nu, with the same quantities forming the new column for the u_nu.
In modern terms this is the period matrix of a genus p+1 surface in which one handle degenerates. The diagonal entry a_{0,0} tends to -infinity. The off-diagonal entries become the differences u_nu(alpha) - u_nu(beta) (up to normalization). That is exactly the period data of a normal integral of the third kind with logarithmic points alpha, beta. Riemann's version is the first (crossed-out) row extended to a full matrix.

(B) Multiplicative theta quotient.
Riemann's theta is theta(v) = sum_n exp(sum a_{mu,nu} n_mu n_nu + 2 sum n_nu v_nu). He forms
F(v) = theta(v - g*pi*i - a.h) / theta(v) * exp(-2 sum_nu v_nu h_nu).
The numerator argument has components w_mu = v_mu - g_mu*pi*i - sum_nu h_nu a_{mu,nu}.
He then sets v_nu = u_nu - sum_{mu=1}^p alpha_nu^mu, the Jacobi-inversion substitution. He states that F gets the factor e^{2 pi i g_nu} at cut a_nu and e^{-2 pi i h_nu} at cut b_nu.
Check (mine):
- theta(v + pi*i e_mu) = theta(v), so the shift by pi*i e_mu multiplies F by e^{-2 pi i h_mu}.
- theta(v + a_{mu,.}) = exp(-a_{mu,mu} - 2 v_mu) theta(v). So the shift by the column a_{mu,.} gives the quotient exp(-2 w_mu + 2 v_mu) = exp(2 pi i g_mu + 2 sum_nu h_nu a_{mu,nu}). The exponential factor contributes exp(-2 sum_nu a_{mu,nu} h_nu), leaving e^{2 pi i g_mu}.
So the factors are right. Which cut carries which factor depends on whether 'an dem Schnitt a_nu' means crossing a_nu (jump = pi*i) or circuit along a_nu. This is a Prym/characteristic-theta function with multipliers, i.e. a section of a flat line bundle.

(C) Degeneration of theta (left middle).
Set a_{1,1} -> -infinity and replace v_nu by v_nu + (1/2) a_{1,nu} for all nu. The exponent of the n-th term contains a_{11}(n_1^2 + n_1) + 2 n_1 v_1 + 2 n_1 sum_{nu>=2} a_{1nu} n_nu + (terms in n_2..n_p).
Since n_1^2 + n_1 >= 0 with equality only at n_1 = 0, -1, only those two summands survive.
- n_1 = 0 gives theta_{p-1}(v_2 + a_{12}/2, ..., v_p + a_{1p}/2).
- n_1 = -1 gives e^{-2 v_1} theta_{p-1}(v_2 + a_{12}/2 - a_{12}, ...) = e^{-2 v_1} theta_{p-1}(v_2 - a_{12}/2, ..., v_p - a_{1p}/2).
Here theta_{p-1} has the (p-1)x(p-1) matrix (a_{mu,nu})_{mu,nu>=2}. Hence
lim theta_p(v + a_{1,.}/2) = theta(v_2 + a_{12}/2, ...) + e^{-2 v_1} theta(v_2 - a_{12}/2, ...),
exactly as written.
Combined with (A), where a_{1,nu} -> alpha_nu - beta_nu, this expresses the theta function of a curve with one pinched cycle (a nodal curve) through the genus p-1 theta function at arguments shifted by plus or minus half the Abel image of alpha - beta.

(D) Right column: local analysis of a singular point (alpha, beta) of a plane curve phi(s,z) = 0.
- Puiseux branch ansatz: s - beta = c_0 (z - alpha)^{m/n} + ...
- Newton-polygon balancing of two monomials (z-alpha)^n (s-beta)^m and (z-alpha)^{n_1} (s-beta)^{m_1} gives the exponent as a ratio of differences.
- Double point: phi = phi_z = phi_s = 0. Tangent directions come from the second-order quadratic phi_zz + 2 s' phi_zs + s'^2 phi_ss = 0, with a third-order term written for a cusp-type case.

(E) Rotated scratch.
There are expansions near z = 0 of a curve phi = f^2 + 2 z f s^{2p-5} + ... and the integral of dz/(d phi/d s). This continues the previous page's integrals of the first kind u = int phi^{n-2} dz / F_s, with adjoint-condition bookkeeping in powers s^{2p-2}, s^{2p-3}, s^{2p-4}. It is too fragmentary to reconstruct with certainty.

Purpose: understanding theta functions of degenerating (singular) curves and of curves with multiple points. Likely this serves Riemann's later work on singular plane curves and the hyperelliptic/special-curve counts on the neighbouring pages.
errors: Newton balancing: from (z-alpha)^n (s-beta)^m = (z-alpha)^{n_1} (s-beta)^{m_1} one gets (z-alpha)^{n-n_1} = (s-beta)^{m_1-m}. Riemann writes (s-beta)^{m-m_1}, and then z-alpha = (s-beta)^{(m-m_1)/(n-n_1)}. This is a sign slip in the exponent, unless the indices were meant with opposite roles; the magnitude of the slope is unaffected.

Multiplier labels: the function as written acquires e^{-2 pi i h} under the shift by pi*i and e^{2 pi i g} under the shift by a_{mu,.}. Attaching e^{2 pi i g} to cut a_nu is consistent with Riemann's 1857 convention only if 'an dem Schnitt a_nu' means circulation along a_nu rather than crossing it. This is a possible label swap, not a mathematical error.
The degeneration step is implicit: the uniform shift of all v_nu by a_{1,nu}/2 and the limit interchange are not justified on the page. The limit is correct termwise and dominated for fixed v.

results.what: Enlarged period scheme: genus p+1 normalized periods in which one row/column becomes the third-kind integral with b-moduli alpha_nu - beta_nu and a_{00} -> -infinity
results.modern_name: Period matrix of a nodal degeneration (pinching a cycle); third-kind differential on the normalization
results.usually_credited_to: Classical degeneration studies (Schottky, Wirtinger c. 1880s-1890s); systematic modern treatment by J. Fay, Theta Functions on Riemann Surfaces (1973)

results.modern_name: Degeneration formula for Riemann theta functions (nodal curve limit)
results.usually_credited_to: Fay 1973 (Ch. III); earlier forms in Wirtinger/Schottky-era literature

results.what: Theta quotient theta(v - g pi i - a h)/theta(v) * exp(-2 v.h), with constant multipliers e^{2 pi i g}, e^{-2 pi i h} across the cuts
results.modern_name: Theta functions with characteristics / multiplicative (Prym) functions; sections of flat line bundles

results.what: Puiseux expansion s - beta = c (z-alpha)^{m/n} via Newton-polygon balancing; double-point conditions phi = phi_z = phi_s = 0 and the tangent quadratic
results.modern_name: Newton-Puiseux method; tangent cone at a singular point

deep.surprise_reason: Theta multipliers and Puiseux analysis are routine for Riemann. The explicit degeneration of the genus-p theta function to theta_{p-1}(v + d/2) + e^{-2v_1} theta_{p-1}(v - d/2), set up from a period scheme with a third-kind integral, is a notable unpublished detail. Such formulas are usually cited from later literature (Fay 1973 and its predecessors). Degeneration ideas are known in Riemann's circle, though, so the result is not a major priority claim.
